the demand control support stress model can explain physician stress and that stress is related to work demands, lack of work control, isolation from colleagues and lack of support for work and home balance.
stress in physicians was related to job demands, control over work, support for balancing home and work, and isolation.

the impact of stress on physicians and the impact of physicians on the quality of care.
how the work of doctors can be improved, so that they can provide better care to their patient and themselves.
the relationship between work environment and stress in physicians.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the demand control model is an excellent way to understand and prevent stress.
stress is a complex phenomenon that is affected by many variables.
physician stress is worsened when physicians have less control over their work and when they have less support in balancing their work and personal lives.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we found that physicians who work in practices where they have more control, more social support, and less isolation have lower levels of stress.

stress is associated with the following: (i) time pressure in patient interactions; (ii) complex case mix; (iii) lack of control over the workplace; (iv) isolation; and (v) lack of support from colleagues and family.
stress is a problem in medicine, but the problem can be addressed.

the stress of the job is a significant factor in the decision to retire early.
the demand-control support model is an important tool for understanding and reducing physician stress.
the stress that physicians experience is not simply a matter of personality or individual coping style but is also a product of the work environment.
